title: Make folder reconnection reliable for newly created named workspaces

needs: Fix the user-reported failure on newly created folder-backed workspaces: Workspace action failed / The workspace folder is unavailable. Reconnect it to save to disk.
Make Reconnect folder restore a usable connection and allow Save and autosave to persist current edits after initial creation, permission loss, missing handle or reload.
Keep all local edits, workspace identity and immutable history safe while reporting permissions, cancellation, access failures and disk durability truthfully.
context: User report on 2026-10-19, repository version 1.19.2. The exact failing browser, permission state and folder selection sequence are not yet known; the error alone does not establish a root cause. Development must reproduce and record the actual path before choosing a fix.

createLineage selects a parent directory, creates a slug subdirectory, writes that child handle to the library, initializes the repository, registers the workspace and reactivates it by reading the handle back. The fresh handle is not retained as the active repository through activation. Investigate handle persistence/readback and failures between initialization and activation; failed setup must not masquerade as successful creation.

resolveDirectory awaits IndexedDB handle retrieval and ensureFolderPermission. relinkFolder awaits that resolution before its repository-open try/catch; permission and handle errors may escape without a usable recovery action. A granted but stale/inaccessible handle leads to repository-open failure without another selection path.

relinkFolder currently accepts only a selected root whose workspace-manifest.json matches workspaceId; creation asked for the parent. Selecting the same parent again is rejected. openFolder already supports roots or immediate child lineages but imports/reconciles them; reconnect must remain scoped to the active identity.

pickLineageFolder is called after asynchronous work in reconnection; ensureFolderPermission may request permission after asynchronous retrieval/querying. Investigate transient user activation with an actual supported browser. All current picker errors except AbortError can be collapsed to null by controller catch handlers, obscuring the cause.

saveNow invokes relinkFolder only when repository is null and substitutes save.error or the generic missing-folder message when reconnect fails. A repository that remains non-null after revoked access is another path to cover. Reconnection currently replaces context.repository and clears error without persisting current edits or re-evaluating dirty/durability against that repository.

The existing folder tests use in-memory File System Access handles and cover creation, parent open and revoked writes, but have no dedicated relinkFolder regression. The current guide records no real OS folder-picker validation. Mock success alone cannot prove activation or persistent handle behavior.

This is a focused reliability follow-up under prod_018 portable lineage contracts and req_168 Settings storage actions. It does not reopen the settled workspace architecture. The companion brief describes only reconnection behavior. Existing working-copy commit verification, read-only protection, session tokens, recovery and conflict handling remain authoritative.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: In a supported secure browser context, create a folder-backed workspace from current content and from empty content, edit and Save immediately, then reload and Save again. The registered workspaceId and slug child root stay stable; successful creation has an accessible initialized repository, and successful saving reads back the expected working file. Handle persistence/readback or setup failures produce an actionable result and recoverable content, never a false fully connected success or duplicate workspace on retry.

AC2: Reconnect handles stored-handle permission states granted/prompt/denied, missing handles, handle retrieval/query/request exceptions and stale handles whose permission is granted but reads fail. Each outcome settles busy state and produces no unhandled rejection. A usable stored handle is reused; unavailable access offers a deliberate Choose folder retry. Picker and permission prompts run from a valid user gesture; if an await consumes activation, show a separate explicit action rather than automatically prompting after that await. Reload never triggers a permission prompt without user action.

AC3: Reconnect accepts the exact lineage root or the original/common parent, using only a unique matching root or immediate child with the active workspaceId. Names and slugs alone never establish identity. Zero matches, multiple matching copies, another workspace, an empty folder or an invalid/unsupported manifest yield precise guidance without changing the connection or writing to candidates. Do not recursively scan the disk, initialize an empty folder or attach a different lineage. Persist the resolved child handle and refresh folderName only after candidate identity and repository validation succeed.

AC4: Reconnection preserves in-memory edits, local recovery, working identity, versions and handoff bytes. It never loads disk content over dirty editor content or changes the technical save base in a way that bypasses conflict detection. If the same-ID disk copy has advanced or diverged from the cached/local base, preserve both heads and use existing conflict/reconciliation choices before saving; never silently overwrite either side. Cancellation, denial, corrupt candidate, read failure or handle persistence failure leave the previous session recoverable and emit no success.

AC5: After successful reconnect, explicitly saving commits the latest editable state through the existing verified write protocol; normal autosave resumes on subsequent edits. Reconnect itself reports connected, not saved. Dirty/error/permission/durability and last durable save time reflect actual operations; no disk-verified claim is made for newer unsaved changes. A write or readback failure keeps dirty/recovery state and a retry action. Save reuses the correct reconnect result instead of replacing cancellation, wrong-folder or permission guidance with the stale generic missing-folder error.

AC6: A delayed picker/permission/repository result for workspace A cannot attach to, alter status for or write editor content from workspace B after switching; repeated clicks and autosave cannot interleave connection commits. Capture active identity/session and recheck across asynchronous boundaries. Reconnect in historical read-only mode cannot persist historical content or bypass existing mutation gates; return to the working copy remains possible. Browser-only workspaces retain browser/ZIP behavior and never receive a folder reconnect requirement.

AC7: Settings > Workspace storage and its recovery notice provide an accessible retry path with the current folder hint and root-or-parent instructions. EN/FR distinguish cancellation (neutral, no failure toast), permission required/denied, unsupported API or insecure context, wrong/missing/ambiguous workspace, read/write failure and successful reconnection. Unsupported folder access explains the existing browser/ZIP alternative without silently migrating storage. Buttons, notice focus targets and Settings search remain usable; expected reconnect states do not show only Workspace action failed.

AC8: Add controller/folder, UI and browser regression evidence mapped to AC1-AC7. Cover fresh creation, reload with persisted handle, revoked/missing/stale handle, root/parent selection, invalid/foreign/duplicate-ID candidates, cancellation, unavailable API, persistence/write/readback failures, dirty/divergent state, workspace switching and historical mode. Record a supported-browser run against a real OS directory picker for create > edit > Save > reload > revoke/regrant or reselect > reconnect > edit > Save > verify disk bytes; if unavailable, record the outstanding limitation and do not claim this evidence completed. Update docs/workspace-lineages.md and pass applicable repository delivery gates before implementation closeout.

product.title: Reliable folder reconnection for named workspace persistence
product.overview: A focused extension of prod_018: a newly created or temporarily disconnected folder-backed workspace can regain access to its own lineage root and save current edits without losing recovery data or claiming unverified disk persistence. Settings explains the next action for each access outcome.
goals: Make create, reconnect, Save and reload a reliable end-to-end folder workflow.
Accept the lineage root or its parent while validating stable workspace identity.
Preserve local and disk work through failed access and divergent copies; provide truthful localized status.
non_goals: New storage modes, cloud sync, account integration or changes to portable schemas.
Moving browser-only workspaces to disk, recreating deleted lineage folders or rebuilding corrupt manifests through reconnect.
Automatic merging, automatic history pruning, recursive disk discovery or broader Settings redesign.

backlog_items.title: Repair named workspace folder connection lifecycle and safe reconnection
problem: New folder-backed workspaces can end up without a usable repository; reconnect may fail before selection, reject the creation parent, hide the cause or leave Save using stale error/status. Existing asynchronous and conflict boundaries must protect edits during recovery.
scope_in: Reproduce the reported error from the Settings create/reconnect/Save paths; record browser/context, actual exception and failing stage. Compare immediate creation with reload and investigate handle storage/readback; identify hypotheses separately from confirmed cause.

Repair creation setup and handle/repository activation sequencing. Preserve a recoverable initialized folder on partial failure and make retry avoid registering duplicate identities or overwriting an existing lineage.

Implement explicit reconnect outcomes and a gesture-safe permission/Choose folder flow, including stale handles and failures before repository.open. Map failures at the originating stage rather than blanket catch-to-null or stale save.error substitution.

Resolve either the selected root or a single immediate child matching workspaceId; reject ambiguity/foreign/invalid folders without writes. Validate before committing the handle, repository and registry folder hint; keep rollback/retry semantics for failed persistence.

Preserve current dirty edits and their disk base, detect changed/divergent same-ID copies and route to existing conservative recovery/conflict behavior. Update status on connection versus actual verified Save; restore subsequent autosave.
Serialize connection commits, guard all asynchronous results by identity/session and retain historical read-only gates. Keep browser-only storage unchanged.

Update EN/FR outcome messages, folder instructions, Settings actions/notices, focus and search labels. Cancel neutrally; describe browser/ZIP fallback for unsupported access without implicit conversion.
scope_out: Portable format changes, new storage modes, deleted-folder recreation, general UI redesign and release publication.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Fresh creation and reload keep a usable stable folder connection or report a recoverable setup failure with no duplicate workspace.
AC2: Permission, retrieval, selection and stale-handle outcomes settle predictably with gesture-safe explicit retries and matching root/parent identity validation.
AC3: Reconnect preserves dirty work and divergent disk heads, cannot cross active-session/read-only boundaries, and reports connected independently from verified Save.
AC4: Save, autosave and localized Settings recovery guidance satisfy request AC1-AC7, including neutral cancellation and browser-only behavior.

backlog_items.title: Validate folder reconnection regressions and document the recovery workflow
problem: Current in-memory folder tests do not exercise reconnect or prove persistent handle and real picker behavior; the reported failure can survive a mock-only fix.
scope_in: Extend existing folder/session fixtures with configurable permission transitions, picker and IndexedDB handle failures, stale granted handles, wrong and duplicate-ID roots, corrupt manifests and failed write/readback. Assert state preservation, file bytes, exact identity and absence of false success, not just result.ok.
Add UI regressions through Settings and recovery notices in EN/FR, including cancel/retry/busy/focus behavior and explicit Save versus reconnect messages.
Exercise real IndexedDB handle persistence in a supported browser where automation permits; test delayed results during switches, repeated clicks, autosave and historical view.

Perform and record the real OS directory picker scenario in request AC8, listing browser/version/context and observed disk verification; retain a clearly outstanding validation item if the environment cannot provide it.

Update docs/workspace-lineages.md with child-root versus parent selection, permission recovery, conflict behavior and browser fallback. Run targeted Vitest/Playwright checks, npm run quality:i18n, lint/typecheck and the repository ci:local delivery gates in the implementation environment; record per-AC evidence and any pre-existing failures.
scope_out: Implementing an unrelated test harness, claiming a mock reproduces real user activation, release publication.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Automated regression evidence maps to request AC1-AC7 and verifies disk bytes, edit/recovery preservation and isolation for the specified failure cases.
AC2: Real-picker validation is recorded with its environment and results, or explicitly outstanding; no unperformed check is marked passed.
AC3: The user guide describes the delivered workflow; applicable quality gates and per-AC delivery evidence are recorded before implementation closeout.

orchestration_task.title: Deliver reliable new workspace folder reconnection
plan: Wave 1: reproduce the exact user-visible failure from a fresh named folder workspace; inspect creation, child-handle persistence, activation, permission and Save paths. Record the verified cause and establish failing regression cases before changing behavior.

Wave 2: deliver backlog item 1 creation and reconnection lifecycle, root/parent resolution, identity checks, conflict-safe preservation and session serialization. Treat candidate validation and handle persistence as a connection commit boundary.

Wave 3: finish explicit gesture-safe retry actions, localized error/status propagation, reconnect versus verified Save semantics and autosave recovery. Verify all request AC1-AC7 boundaries with focused tests.

Wave 4: deliver backlog item 2 automated coverage and actual supported-browser OS picker verification, docs and applicable repository gates. Record request AC1-AC8 evidence and any outstanding environment limitations before closeout.
Leave the chain unimplemented and ready for development after scoping; start, progress and close it only through lifecycle commands during actual implementation.
